# Ensuring Vaccine Integrity in Transit

Ilsabet Naskmere: Welcome back to The Pyrlet Hour, everyone. Today, we’re diving into a crucial topic—keeping vaccines safe on their journey from factory to pharmacy. I’m joined by Orsin Naskvane, who’s spent the last decade pioneering cold-chain logistics in the pharmaceutical sector. Orsin, great to have you here.

Orsin Naskvane: Thanks, Ilsabet. It’s a pleasure.

Ilsabet Naskmere: Let’s start with why this matters. You once told me about a shipment of a new flu vaccine that arrived spoiled despite strict protocols. What happened there?

Orsin Naskvane: Right, that was in 2021. The shipment was routed through a regional hub that lacked real-time temperature monitoring. The vaccine crates were stored in a container where the cooling system failed overnight, and no alarms were triggered until it was too late. It ultimately cost the company $2.3 million in losses and delayed distribution by weeks.

Ilsabet Naskmere: That’s a huge hit. How have innovations changed the game since then?

Orsin Naskvane: Sensor tags have become smarter and more connected. We now use multi-sensor tags that track not just temperature, but also humidity and shock. They relay data via satellite, so logistics teams get instant alerts. In a recent trial shipping a COVID-19 booster, a damaged pallet was detected immediately, preventing compromised doses from reaching clinics.

Ilsabet Naskmere: Fascinating. So, it’s a blend of tech and vigilant oversight that’s really moving the needle?

Orsin Naskvane: Exactly. The future lies in integrating these systems with AI to predict risks before they happen and optimize routes dynamically. It’s about turning data into actionable insights to protect public health.
